comparison: Perfect agreement on literature analysis claims (C23-C27, C83-C91). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED with similar reasoning. OpenEval emphasizes systematic methodology and sample sizes, while peer reviewers praised the analysis as 'very clever' and 'comprehensive.' No disagreements identified.

Complete agreement on ECG analysis findings (C28-C30). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the large sample sizes and appropriately documented exception in C29. Peer reviewers acknowledged these findings as part of comprehensive demonstration without challenge.

Full concordance on TRF analysis showing residual ECG after ICA (C31-C36, C55, C67). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from encoding/decoding models. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed findings, noting cardiac activity remains 'even after applying ICA analysis' and 'even after applying a very sensitive threshold.'

Strong agreement on MEG findings and spatial effects (C37-C43). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers broader claim set including control analyses (C70-C71, C92-C97) while peer R4 focuses on core age-related findings. Peer reviewers praised 'multiverse approach' and replication efforts as 'commendable.'

Partial overlap on control analyses (C70-C71, C97). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval R4 includes these as part of comprehensive MEG analysis. Peer R7 specifically addresses control analyses with minor concern about head movement as proxy for muscle activity, but concludes it wouldn't reverse conclusions.

Partial overlap on replication and validation (C92-C94). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval R4 includes these within broader MEG findings. Peer R8 specifically praises replication across datasets and algorithms as 'commendable and highly valuable to the community.'

Partial overlap on age-related effects and cardiac contributions (C44-C46). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 focuses on multiple regression showing independence of neural vs cardiac effects. Peer R4 addresses these claims within broader context of comprehensive MEG analysis and multiverse approach.

Partial overlap on main research question (C7-C8). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 emphasizes statistical methodology testing independence. Peer R5 focuses on main conclusions (C5-C6, C58) with editor stating study 'provides compelling evidence' and reviewers concluding age effects 'can mainly be explained by cardiac activity.'

Perfect agreement on working memory analysis (C47-C49). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes clear statistical evidence and dose-response relationship but mentions modest sample size. Peer reviewer enthusiastically endorsed this analysis, stating it 'practically warrants a separate paper its own!'

Complete claim overlap (C50-C54, C98-C102) but different evaluations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are 'primarily speculative' or based on citations rather than direct evidence. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'thorough discussion' and that 'authors address this issue in their discussion.' Disagreement on whether speculative mechanisms warrant SUPPORTED vs UNCERTAIN.

Near-complete overlap on background claims (C1-C3, C9-C22, C74). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these establish 'well-documented background knowledge' from prior literature. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted foundation by not challenging background, focusing instead on novel findings. Minor difference: peer R12 includes C72-C73 which OpenEval places in R12.

Perfect agreement on E/I balance and drug effects discussion (C60-C68). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about drug effects being conflated by cardiac activity. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with one 'very much appreciating' the commentary on pharmacological challenges. Disagreement on evaluation type despite same claims.

Complete agreement on sample description and methodology (C4, C75-C82). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes clear documentation and appropriate noting of limitations. Peer reviewers praised 'large sample sizes' and 'methodological rigor' with no concerns about sample characteristics or ethics.

Partial overlap on main conclusions (C5-C6, C58). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval R11 identifies these as main conclusions directly supported by TRF and regression analyses. Peer R5 provides explicit endorsement from all reviewers and editor, with strong statements about 'compelling evidence' for cardiac contributions to age effects.

Partial overlap on methodological context (C56-C57, C69, C72-C73, C103-C104). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these provide important methodological context from prior work. Peer R12 includes only C72-C73 from this set, implicitly accepting citation-based methodological foundation without challenge.

Perfect agreement on recommendations (C105-C106). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes recommendations 'logically follow' from findings about ICA limitations and current practice gaps. Peer reviewer explicitly endorsed recommendations as 'very helpful,' and editor noted 'important implications for all future research.'
